title: The format page says how records are kept, then indexes kinds, relations and checks
statement: The format page (`?page=format`) MUST say how records are kept, then show an index: the kinds by stage, the relations with their words read both ways, and the checks under Errors and Warnings. Kinds and checks MUST be clickable rows leading to their pages.

title: Format pages open in the wiki card over the stage
statement: Each format page MUST open in the wiki card, the whole page, over the current focus (`?page=format/…`), the stage keeping its focus behind it (a bottom sheet on a phone), with a link back to the focus's own page. Collapsing the card, Escape or moving to another focus MUST close it.

title: A kind page shows everything the reference says about the kind, with a real example
statement: A kind's page (`?page=format/kinds/<kind>`) MUST show its description; its stage; its allowed parents and children as links to their kind pages; its columns, each with its type, whether it is required, its meaning and its own anchor; its obligation, its ID pattern and its ID scope; the relations out of it and into it by their readable labels, each naming the kind at the other end; and the checks that concern it. It MUST show the product's first record of the kind with a link to it, and the count of the product's records of the kind, with a row per parent leading to that parent's group of them.

title: Every kind and every check has one page, from the product's own data
statement: The kinds, relations, folders and checks the reference pages show MUST be the product's own: the schema with its product kinds, and Lathe's check rows with the product's. The pages MUST be built from the loaded data; a check that reports problems but has no row is the engine's own, listed without an explanation. Each kind MUST have one page at `?page=format/kinds/<kind>` and each check one page at `?page=format/checks/<check>`, on whatever focus the stage shows, named by the kind's or check's name as records and problems carry it. A name the format does not know MUST say so, with a link to the format page.

title: A check page shows its explanation, its query and the problems it reports now
statement: A check's page (`?page=format/checks/<check>`) MUST show its severity, its summary and explanation (rendered Markdown), where it comes from and its query, the kinds it concerns, and the current space's problems with that code as clickable rows.

title: The Changes panel lists the changes newest first, by record, as cards
statement: The Changes panel MUST list the records changed since the baseline, newest first (those that changed while the page was open by when they landed, then the rest by ID), by record, each a card naming its kind, ID and title, what changed and when, and its fields old → new. Clicking a card MUST focus its record on the stage, the panel staying open with that card marked; a removed record's card MUST show what it was instead, since it has no page.

title: Its toggle shows how many records changed
statement: The Changes panel's toggle, among every stage's Changes controls, MUST show how many records changed since the baseline, and its accessible name MUST say it in words.

title: The Checks panel lists its product's problems, errors first, grouped by check
statement: The Checks panel MUST list every problem of its space's product, errors before warnings, grouped by check, then the problems that belong to no product (data the store refuses, a check that could not run) under a Workspace heading, which every space's panel shows. It MUST NOT list another product's problems. Selecting a problem MUST focus its record on the stage, which the wiki card then shows, while the panel stays open with that record's rows marked, to work down the list. A problem that names no record MUST open its check's page in the wiki card instead.

title: A problem's code leads to its check
statement: Wherever a problem's check code is shown, in the Checks panel and on a record's page, it MUST be a link that opens that check's page in the wiki card.

title: Each space has its own Checks panel
statement: The Checks panel MUST list the current space's problems only, opened over the stage from the nav's Tools and by the Checks shortcuts (`?panel=checks`), and stay open, showing the new space's problems, when the Reader moves to another focus or space; there MUST be no Checks list for every product at once.

title: The Checks panel lists its recorded exceptions in their own section
statement: The Checks panel MUST list its product's recorded exceptions (each command that also changes another aggregate in the same transaction, and each repository that also persists another aggregate) in a section of their own, titled Recorded exceptions, each naming the command or repository, the aggregate and the reason. They MUST NOT be shown or counted as problems.

title: The product page shows each domain with its coverage
statement: The product page MUST show each domain as a card that opens the domain page wherever it is clicked, with one group of small bars per obligation kind the engine reports for it, labeled with the kind's label and in the engine's order, each with designed, built, proved and not-automated-yet counts. It MUST NOT name obligation kinds of its own, and a count the engine does not report MUST NOT be shown as zero.

title: The product page lists its open questions and problems
statement: The product page MUST list the product's open questions, with their owners, and the problems found in its records.

title: The product page sums up what Lathe counts across the product
statement: The product page MUST show, in a Summary section, what Lathe counts across the product's domains: designed, built and proved, totaled over every obligation kind; the not-automated-yet count on its own line, apart from proved; a Tests row totaling its domains' tests by state; its open questions; and its errors and warnings. A product with nothing to count MUST show zeros, not an empty section.

title: Each domain card shows its tests by state
statement: Each domain card MUST show the domain's tests by state under its bars, such as `Tests 12 automated, 1 manual, 2 not automated yet`, from `Coverage.tests`.

title: The product page lists its business outcomes first
statement: The product page MUST list its business outcomes before its domains, in the discovery stage's color, each a card that opens the outcome wherever it is clicked, with its statement, measure and target and the capabilities that serve it, saying so when none does; Shared MUST NOT list them again.

title: An open page loads the data again when it changes, at the same address
statement: When the server sends `spec:changed`, an open page MUST load the data again without a manual refresh, staying at the same address.

title: A panel's edge resizes it by drag or keyboard
statement: The inner edge of each resizable floating panel (the navigation and the wiki card) MUST be a handle that resizes it when dragged, and when focused MUST step with the arrow keys (bigger steps with Shift) and jump to the limits with Home and End, the arrow toward the panel shrinking it. Each size MUST stay within its limits: the navigation 256 to 560 px and the wiki card 360 to 900 px.

title: Sizes are remembered, and double-click resets one
statement: Each panel's size MUST be remembered (the navigation's across visits, the wiki card's for the session), a remembered size outside its limits MUST fall back to the default, and double-clicking a handle MUST reset its panel to the default: the navigation 336 px, the wiki card a third of the open space.

title: Dragging the navigation small folds it
statement: Dragging the navigation below 180 px MUST fold it to its rail; dragging the rail's gap out again MUST unfold the navigation. On a narrow screen there MUST be no gaps to drag: the navigation is a sheet.

title: Hiding a panel gives its space to the stage and loses nothing
statement: Hiding the nav or the wiki card MUST give its space to the stage, which frames the focus again in the open space it leaves, and MUST keep a control that brings it back: the nav keeps its rail, and the wiki card's toggle sits at the right of the page bar, as VS Code's layout toggles do, never as a full-height strip. The wiki card and the header strip MUST describe the same page whichever stage shows, so hiding a panel never hides the record's facts for good.

title: A theme applies at once and before first paint
statement: Choosing a theme or a mode MUST apply at once, without a reload. On load, the chosen theme and mode MUST be on the page before the first paint, so it never flashes another theme.

title: One keymap table drives the keys, the palette and the sheet
statement: Every keyboard command MUST be one row in one table (command id, title, group, default keys, where it applies), and the key handlers, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST all be drawn from it, so nothing is listed twice. "Mod" MUST mean Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere, in matching and in what the app shows (⌘⇧P on a Mac, Ctrl+Shift+P elsewhere).

title: The default shortcuts follow VS Code
statement: The defaults MUST be: Cmd/Ctrl+P and Cmd/Ctrl+K quick open; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P the command palette; Cmd/Ctrl+B the nav; Enter and Ctrl+W (Alt+W off a Mac) to show or collapse the wiki card, and Escape to collapse it (`LA-V96-R19`); Ctrl+G (Alt+G) or Ctrl+1, Ctrl+E (Alt+E) or Ctrl+2, and Ctrl+T (Alt+T) or Ctrl+3 the Graph, ERD and Trace stages; Escape to clear or close the innermost thing; Ctrl+- and Ctrl+Shift+- back and forward (Alt+Left and Alt+Right left to the browser); F12 open the focused link's record; Shift+F12 the wiki card's whole page, with focus moved to its incoming links; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M Checks; F8 and Shift+F8 the next and previous problem on the page; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E focus the nav; `/` the nearest search box; `?` and Cmd/Ctrl+/ the shortcuts sheet; on the graph `+` and `-` depth, `v` the other of the Tree and Nested layouts, `.` fit, the arrow keys, or W, A, S and D as Up, Left, Down and Right, to step through the tree (Left out and Right in in the Tree layout, Up out and Down in in the Nested layout, the other two across; `LA-V93-R19`) and Enter to focus the box with keyboard focus (on the focus's own box, the wiki card); and `g` then `c`, `f` or `h` for Checks, the format and home, with a small hint while the second key is awaited.

title: Shortcuts never get in the way of typing or of the browser
statement: Single-key shortcuts MUST NOT fire while typing; the app MUST call preventDefault only for keys it handles (so Cmd/Ctrl+P never opens the print dialog, and unhandled keys reach the browser); and no binding MUST take a browser essential. A shortcut without Ctrl, Cmd or Alt (a letter, a symbol, a sequence such as `g c`) MUST NOT fire while focus is in a text input, a text area, a select or editable text. A plain Enter MUST stay with a control that handles Enter itself, and Escape with a text field. Alt+Left and Alt+Right still go back and forward.

title: A person can change the bindings
statement: The app MUST read optional overrides from local storage (`lathe:keybindings`, a JSON map of command id to a binding or a list of bindings), ignore unknown commands and bad values, and say how in the shortcuts sheet, with each command's id shown.

title: Every command works without a mouse and is announced
statement: Every command MUST be reachable from the keyboard, and a command that changes what shows (a stage switch, a panel shown or hidden, the next problem) MUST be announced to screen readers through a polite live region.

title: A command's keys suit the platform
statement: A command MAY have other keys off a Mac. On a Mac, Ctrl means the Control key, so Ctrl+W leaves Cmd+W to the browser; elsewhere Ctrl+W closes the tab, Ctrl+G finds the next match and Ctrl+T opens a tab, so the wiki card and the stages take Alt+W, Alt+G, Alt+E and Alt+T there. In the desktop app Cmd or Ctrl+W and T belong to the menu's Close Tab and New Tab (`LA-V96-R17`). A binding that is reserved for the browser on the current platform MUST never be offered, even through an override, and tooltips, `aria-keyshortcuts`, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST show the keys for the current platform.

title: A tooltip shows the control and its keys
statement: Every icon button and control that has a shortcut MUST show it in its tooltip as its name then its keys ("Show or hide the navigation ⌘B", or "Ctrl+B" off a Mac), after a short hover delay and at once on keyboard focus.

title: A control with a shortcut has aria-keyshortcuts
statement: Every control with a shortcut MUST carry `aria-keyshortcuts` with its keys.

title: Every hint reads from the keymap
statement: Every shortcut hint (tooltip, palette row, sheet row, `aria-keyshortcuts`, placeholder) MUST be read from the one keymap with the person's overrides applied, so a rebinding changes every hint; no hint is written by hand.

title: A tooltip never gets in the way
statement: At most one tooltip MUST show at a time; a click or a page moving focus on load MUST NOT open one; Escape, leaving the control or moving focus away MUST close it.

title: Below 900 px wide the app has a compact top bar and fits the screen
statement: Below 900 px wide the app MUST take its phone layout. Its top bar MUST hold the menu button, the page's title on one line (cut with an ellipsis) under a link one step up (to the record's parent, a domain's product, or all products, keeping the view in front), and a quick find button. The layout MUST fill the screen's dynamic height (`100dvh`), keep its bars and sheets clear of the safe areas (`env(safe-area-inset-*)`, with `viewport-fit=cover`), and no page MUST scroll sideways at 320 px wide.

title: A phone keeps the stage filling the screen, switched from the page bar
statement: On a phone a record, group, product or domain page MUST show its stage filling the screen under the top bar and a compact page bar, with no resize handles: in the desktop app the Open pages button, then the stage switch (Graph, ERD and Trace, one pressed) and the wiki card button. Switching the stage MUST name it in the address (`?stage=erd`) and keep it in the place. The wiki card MUST open as a bottom sheet, on demand (`LA-V61-R20`).

title: The nav is a full-screen sheet with the same rows, sized for a thumb
statement: On a phone the nav MUST open from the top bar's menu button as a full-screen sheet that slides in from the left, keeps the space rail, takes focus to its quick find, keeps Tab inside it, and closes by Escape, its close button or choosing a page, giving focus back to the menu button. Its rows MUST be the wide screen's rows (`LA-V90-R03`), at least 44 px tall on a touch screen, with the fold chevrons as large targets.

title: The wiki card is a bottom sheet on a phone
statement: On a phone the wiki card MUST open as a bottom sheet over the stage, at half height, with a dimmed backdrop: it takes focus as it opens, keeps Tab inside it, and closes on Escape, a tap on the backdrop, a swipe down or its own close button, giving focus back to the control that opened it. A drag on its handle MUST take it to full height and back, settling by distance and speed.

title: In the desktop app, the open pages are a sheet
statement: On a phone-sized window of the desktop app the tabs MUST fold into an Open pages button in the page bar that shows how many are open and opens them as a bottom sheet: one row per tab with its ID and title, the active one marked, and a close button on every row. Choosing a row MUST go to that tab and close the sheet. The web app has no tabs of its own, so no Open pages button (`LA-V96-R32`).

title: Quick find opens at the top on a phone
statement: On a phone quick find, and the command palette it turns into after a ">", MUST open from the top bar (and from their shortcuts) as a full-width sheet at the top of the screen over the dimmed stage: the search box at the top with a Close button, the results as a list under it, each title wrapping rather than cut. Choosing a result MUST go there and close the sheet; Escape, Close or a tap on the stage MUST close it and give focus back. The shortcuts sheet MUST fill the screen.

title: The graph and the ERD pan, pinch and take taps
statement: The graph and the ERD MUST pan with a finger and zoom with a pinch. On a touch screen a first tap on a node MUST select it: the node is outlined and a card at the bottom of the canvas shows its kind and name; a second tap on it, or a tap anywhere on the card, MUST open it; a tap on the empty canvas MUST let it go. A click with a mouse MUST still open a node at once. A long press does nothing of its own: the tap's card is the preview.

title: Pages are readable on a phone
statement: On a phone body text MUST be at least 16 px, and every text box MUST be 16 px so the phone does not zoom in on focus. Long IDs MUST wrap rather than widen the page; wide tables and code blocks MUST scroll sideways inside their own box; long lists MUST keep their ten rows with a search (`LA-TRC-SP02`). A record row MUST stack: its ID on a line of its own, its title under it at the row's full width, and its meta (counts, tags, marks) below, so a title is never squeezed beside an ID.

title: The browser chrome follows the theme, and sheets move only when motion is welcome
statement: The page MUST carry a `theme-color` meta that follows the theme's sheet color, in light and dark and for any theme chosen. Sheets MUST slide in with the shared motion tokens and MUST appear at once when the system asks for reduced motion (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R04`).

title: A tablet in landscape keeps the workbench, sized for touch
statement: The screen's width MUST decide the layout and the pointer the size of targets: at 900 px and wider, a tablet MUST keep the floating panels over the stage (nav, tab panel, wiki card), with every target at least 44 × 44 px on a touch screen (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07`); below 900 px, a tablet in portrait MUST take the phone layout.

title: The first load shifts nothing
statement: When a product, domain or record page first loads, nothing already drawn MAY move: content that arrives late (the specs, the fonts) MUST take room kept for it or appear without pushing what is drawn. The nav draws its lists once the specs have arrived; the fonts are the app's own, preloaded, and a font that is not there in time is not swapped in later.

title: Moving between records keeps the frame still
statement: Moving to another record through the nav, a link, a click on the stage, Back or quick find MUST keep the nav, the tab panel and the wiki card where they were, and MUST draw the new page at its place from its first frame: the wiki card's new page at the top, and a page reached by Back or Forward where it was scrolled. The nav's rows, the stage switch and the tabs' close buttons MUST NOT move: the stage switch holds the same three buttons on every page, and every tab has one width.

title: Collapsing or resizing a panel moves only it, and recenters the stage
statement: Showing, collapsing or resizing the nav or the wiki card MUST change only that panel: the other panels stay, the stage is not drawn anew, and the stage frames its focus again in the new open space with a short camera move on the shared motion (at once under reduced motion).

title: Folding moves only what is below the row
statement: Opening or closing a row, and Expand all or Collapse all, MUST move only what is below the row or the list; the row itself, the lists above it and the page title stay, and nothing jumps and then corrects.

title: Resizing follows the pointer
statement: Dragging a gap MUST resize what sits beside it with the pointer and never jump back to a size it left; folding a panel by drag moves nothing on the far side of the page.

title: The graph and the ERD stage keep their canvas still
statement: Re-centering the graph at any depth, changing the depth, and moving between a domain's, an aggregate's and an entity's ERD MUST keep the header strip, the stage's tools and the canvas at one size and place; only the boxes and the camera move, on the shared motion.

title: A live reload keeps what is in view
statement: When the specs reload while the Reader is scrolled part-way down, what was at the top of the view MUST stay there, and the graph MUST NOT be drawn anew.

title: Overlays are placed before they show
statement: A tooltip, quick find, the command palette and the shortcuts sheet MUST be placed before they show and stay where they showed; typing in their search box filters the list under it without moving the box.

title: Switching theme moves nothing
statement: Switching the theme MUST change colors only: no box moves or changes size.

title: The mobile sheets move nothing behind them
statement: At phone width (375 px), opening and closing the nav and wiki card sheets MUST NOT move the page behind them.

title: Moving around answers within the performance budgets
statement: Opening a record page, switching views and re-centering the graph MUST answer within the app's performance budgets (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11`): the page is interactive within 1.5 s, a view switch takes under 100 ms of main-thread work, and a re-center at depth 3 glides at 60 Hz, with at most 3 frames over 20 ms and none of 100 ms or more, so the shared motion keeps gliding while the new picture arrives.

title: The frame of a page holds still
statement: The nav, the tab panel, the wiki card and the stage MUST keep their place and size unless the Reader moves or resizes them; a change of page changes what they show, not where they are. Content that arrives after the page is drawn (the specs, the fonts, what the stage tells the header strip) MUST take room kept for it, arrive before paint, or be drawn where it pushes nothing the Reader can see.

title: A bar keeps one height, and a scroll box its gutter
statement: A bar that must not move (the header strip, every stage's toolbar) MUST have a fixed block size, or be one line cut with an ellipsis whose whole text is its tooltip, and text that changes in it MUST be one text, so a new number never moves what follows. A box that scrolls up and down MUST keep room for its scrollbar (`scrollbar-gutter: stable`), so its content keeps its width when the scrollbar comes and goes.

title: Every page passes the audit
statement: The product, domain, record and group pages on each stage with the panels open and collapsed, Checks, Format and Appearance, quick find, the command palette, the shortcuts sheet, a tooltip and the phone's drawers and sheets MUST pass axe-core's WCAG 2.2 AA rules, at 1440 px and at 375 px, in the Lathe theme and the High contrast theme, each in light and in dark, and under reduced transparency.

title: Every control is reached and worked by the keyboard
statement: Tab and Shift+Tab MUST reach every control a page draws, each with a visible focus ring, and go all the way round the page and back without being held anywhere. Inside a group of controls (the tab strip, a tree's rows) the arrow keys move and Enter or Space acts; in the graph, Tab moves between the boxes; elsewhere the arrow keys walk the stage by its keys (Left out and Right in in the Tree view, Up out and Down in in the Nested view; `LA-V93-R19`, `LA-V61-R49`). The main tasks MUST work by keyboard alone: open a record from the nav or from quick find, switch views, re-center the graph, fold and unfold a row, collapse and show the wiki card, and pick a theme.

title: Focus lands where the Reader expects
statement: After a move to another page, focus MUST stay on the page, never fall to the body. A control that changes the page in place (a stage switch, a panel toggle, a fold button) MUST keep focus, and a panel collapsed from inside it MUST give focus to its toggle. Re-centering the graph by keyboard MUST put focus on the box that became the center. A dialog (quick find, the palette, the shortcuts sheet, the theme picker), a phone sheet (the wiki card, quick find, and in the desktop app the open pages) or a drawer (the nav) MUST take focus when it opens, keep Tab inside it while it is open, and give focus back to the control that opened it when it closes.

title: What changes out of sight is announced
statement: When a command changes the page somewhere other than where focus is (a stage switched, the wiki card shown or collapsed, a theme chosen, every row folded), the app's one announcer (a polite live region) MUST say so in a short sentence, such as "Graph stage", "Wiki card collapsed" or "Color theme: Midnight".

title: A control's name holds its visible text
statement: A control's accessible name MUST contain the text it shows, so a person who says what they see, or hears the name read, finds the same control. Where a control shows a count or a mark, the name is built from what is shown, with words for a screen reader added beside it in hidden text (`sr-only`), rather than an `aria-label` that says something else: the nav's Checks row is named "Checks 3 errors 12 warnings", and a space's button, which shows a monogram the reader is not meant to hear, is named by its product's title in hidden text, with the mark hidden. An `aria-label` that stays MUST include the shown text as a word: "Open pages: 2".

title: No control inside another
statement: A control MUST NOT hold another control: a screen reader reads the outer one as one thing and cannot reach the inner one. Where two act on one item, they sit side by side in a plain wrapper, as a page tab and its close button do.

title: A box that scrolls can be reached by keyboard
statement: A box that scrolls on its own and holds nothing that takes focus (a code block, a stage's key bar, the shortcuts sheet's groups) MUST take focus itself (`tabindex="0"`) and be named as a region, so the arrow keys can scroll it.

title: A target is at least 24 px, or has room around it
statement: On any pointer, a link or control that is not inside a sentence MUST be at least 24 by 24 px, or stand far enough from its neighbors that a 24 px circle on it touches no other target (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.8). Record links listed in a table cell or the wiki card are drawn one line tall at 24 px. On a coarse pointer the larger 44 px of `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07` applies.

title: Text sits only on the surfaces the theme vouches for
statement: Body text and muted text MUST be drawn only on the surfaces whose contrast every built-in theme guarantees: the page (`--paper`) and a sheet (`--sheet`), which the theme contrast audit (`app/src/theme/audit.ts`) holds to 4.5:1 in light and dark. The shell (`--shell`) is the gap between panels and holds no text: a page that is one panel, such as Checks or Appearance, draws its own `--paper` background rather than let the shell show through.

title: The arrows, WASD and Shift+Up and Shift+Down walk every stage's levels, except in arrow controls
statement: On a record, group, product or domain page, the stage walk MUST move over the stage shown (Graph, ERD or Trace) from anywhere on the page, without the stage having keyboard focus first: the plain arrow keys, with the plain letters W, A, S and D doing exactly what Up, Left, Down and Right do, and Shift+Up (or Shift+W) going out to the container and Shift+Down (or Shift+S) in to the first node inside it, the same on every stage, the Graph included, as the stage toolbar's buttons do (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R21`); all through the same walk and the same guard, each move moving the stage's focus as a click does. Each stage MUST be walked as a hierarchy: the Graph its tree; the ERD the product, each domain's region, each aggregate's area and each entity; the Trace its tree, each copy of a record in its own place. An arrow MUST move among the siblings, the nodes of one level in the same container: on the Graph and the Trace by the layout's keys (`LA-V93-R19`, the Trace as the Graph's Tree); on the ERD by where the boxes sit on the map, never by the record tree. At a container's edge an arrow MUST go on to the next container's first node at that level in reading order (left to right, top to bottom) going Right or Down, or to the previous container's last going Left or Up, so repeated presses visit every node at a level; from the product an arrow goes in, Right and Down to its first node and Left and Up to its last. On the ERD an arrow MUST go to the nearest sibling that way by the boxes' centers: those overlapping the current box's row (Left and Right) or column (Up and Down) first, then the shortest distance. Faded boxes count: a step into a faded area brings it into focus. A focus that picks out no box walks from its domain's region. On the Trace stage a record several chains hold MUST keep the copy the walk arrived on, and Enter on a link MUST focus the capability it leads to; on a box that is no record (a gap, a file, a link, the Untraced mark) the walk MUST move the keyboard's ring, announced, and leave the focus where it is. One handler in the commands layer MUST do it for every stage. A plain arrow, one of those letters, or Shift with Up, Down, W or S, MUST stay with the element that has keyboard focus when that element uses arrows itself (so a letter is always typed where text is taken): a text field, a textarea, a select, editable text (the chat's message box), a radio group, a slider, a focusable splitter (a panel's resize handle), a menu or menu button, a listbox or combobox (quick find, the command palette, the theme picker), a tab list, a modal dialog, a box that took focus to scroll by them (`LA-V61-R46`), and an element marked as handling arrows itself (a tree list's rows, the chat log, the breadcrumb's menu, and the Trace table under its canvas). The nav's links do not use arrows: with one focused, as after a click in the nav, the arrows walk the stage. Arrows and letters with Cmd, Ctrl or Alt MUST keep their own meanings, and Shift with Left, Right, A or D does nothing new. Clicked into, the wiki card MUST NOT scroll by the arrows; Page Up, Page Down, Space and the pointer still scroll them. When a step leaves keyboard focus where it was (anywhere but a graph box, from which focus follows to the new focus's box and is read out there), the new focus MUST be announced in the page's live region by its kind and title.

title: Appearance lists the themes, each previewed live on the stage
statement: Appearance MUST open as a popover over the stage from its button at the foot of the nav, and from the command palette ("Open Appearance settings"), at `?panel=appearance` on the current focus. It MUST offer light, dark or system, and list every theme, built in and the Reader's own, each with a chip of its colors, the one in use marked: pointing at or focusing a theme MUST preview it live on the whole app, the stage included, and clicking it MUST keep it. Each theme MUST have a button to duplicate and edit it (built in) or edit it (the Reader's own), and to export it.

title: A copy of a theme can be edited, renamed, reset and deleted
statement: "Duplicate and edit" MUST make a copy and open it in the theme editor, a larger panel over the stage (`?panel=theme&theme=<id>`), with: color pickers grouped by purpose (surfaces, text, borders, accent, signals, graph and depth), the light and dark sets side by side; fonts for headings, text and code from a short safe list or a custom font stack; text size, density (comfortable or compact), panel corner radius, gap between panels, and motion (follow the system or always reduced). The theme being edited MUST be the one in use, so the app around the editor is its live preview, beside small light and dark previews. The editor MUST rename the theme, reset it to the built-in it was copied from, and delete it after asking, going back to Appearance.

title: Hard-to-read colors are flagged while editing
statement: While editing, each text or control color whose contrast on what it is drawn on falls below WCAG AA (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and controls) MUST show a warning beside its swatch, with the ratio, the background and the ratio it needs, for the mode it fails in.

title: Themes are kept per person and travel as files
statement: The reader's own themes, the chosen theme and the mode MUST be kept per person (in the browser's local storage, behind a store the desktop app can replace), and MUST survive a reload. Any theme MUST export as a small, versioned JSON file, and such a file MUST import as a new theme of his own.

title: The Color theme command previews each theme and keeps or puts back
statement: The "Color theme" command (`chooseTheme`, g then t) MUST open a quick pick of every theme. Arrowing to a theme MUST show it on the whole app at once, without keeping it; Enter or a click MUST keep it, and Escape or a click outside MUST put back the theme shown before.

title: Light, dark or system is chosen in the app
statement: Every theme MUST show its light or dark set by the person's choice of System (the default, following `prefers-color-scheme`), Light or Dark. The choice MUST be made by the "Light, dark or system" command (`chooseColorMode`), which previews like the theme picker, and on Appearance.

title: Quick find and the command palette are one overlay; the shortcuts sheet is searchable
statement: Cmd/Ctrl+P (or Cmd/Ctrl+K) MUST open one search box in the upper middle of the window over a lightly dimmed stage, on records; a query that starts with ">" (or opening it with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P) MUST list every command that applies on the current page instead, filtered as the Reader types, and deleting the ">" MUST go back to records. A command MUST apply only while what it acts on is shown: a stage hidden while the next one loads MUST stop answering its commands at once, and answer again once shown. Up and Down MUST move through the results, Enter MUST go to the record or run the command, and Escape or a click on the dimmed stage MUST close it. The nav's "Go to…" button with its shortcut hint, the rail's Quick find button, the phone's top bar and the desktop command center MUST open it. The shortcuts sheet MUST list every shortcut grouped as Navigate, View, Graph and Lists, with a search box. Both MUST be dialogs that take focus, keep Tab inside, close with Escape and give focus back.

title: Menus and quick find's commands show each command's keys at the right
statement: Quick find's commands, and any menu, MUST show each command's first shortcut right-aligned on its row in `<kbd>` styling; a command without one shows none.

title: Quick find jumps to anything by ID or title
statement: Quick find MUST find any record, domain or product by ID or title, best matches first (exact ID, ID prefix, title), and MUST let the Reader move through the results with the arrow keys and open one with Enter. Each record result MUST show its kind chip, its ID and its title, and a short trail of the places above it in the one breadcrumb's collapsed form (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R16`), so similar titles can be told apart.

title: Quick find searches the current space only
statement: Quick find MUST search only the current space's records (and the record format's kinds and checks), as one list for the arrow keys, and MUST NOT list anything of another product: switching product is the rail's job.

title: Quick find finds kinds and checks
statement: Quick find MUST list every kind as "Kind: <label>" and every check as "Check: <name>", found by their names and labels, each leading to its page.

title: A highlighted record previews on the stage
statement: While a record result is highlighted and the highlight rests, the stage MUST glide to it and the wiki card MUST show it in its compact summary, without moving the address, the tabs, the header strip or the card's own More or Less setting. Enter MUST commit (the address moves there); Escape or any other close MUST return the camera, the wiki card (with its scroll and setting) and keyboard focus to where they were. Under reduced motion the stage MUST move at once, with no glide. A command, or a page of the record format, MUST NOT preview.

title: Quick open is an accessible dialog
statement: Quick open MUST be a modal dialog named for its mode (Quick find, or Command palette) holding a combobox that controls a listbox and names the highlighted option with `aria-activedescendant`; keyboard focus MUST stay in the box while the arrows move the highlight, and MUST return to where it was when it closes. Its text and chips MUST pass AA contrast in every look. Arrow keys pressed in its box MUST move its highlight only, never the stage.

title: The shortcuts sheet matches the hints
statement: The shortcuts sheet (`?`) MUST list the same keys the hints show, with one "Switch to <product>" row per product that has a key.

title: The record format is a command and a link in the shortcuts sheet
statement: The record format MUST NOT be a link in the nav's footer or rail. It MUST be the "Record format" command in the command palette (g then f) and a link in the shortcuts sheet; the desktop app's Help menu has an entry too. The footer MUST keep saying where the data comes from.

title: The menus are File, Edit, View, Window and Help
statement: The shell MUST have native menus: File (Open Product Folder…, Open Recent, Close Window), Edit, View (the app commands, then Reload, Force Reload, Toggle Developer Tools, the zoom items and Toggle Full Screen), Window, and Help (Record Format, Keyboard Shortcuts), with the app menu first on a Mac.

title: A menu choice runs the app command by its ID
statement: A menu item for an app command MUST send the command's ID from the keymap (such as `stageGraph` or `toggleNav`) to the page, and the app's command system MUST run it, as if its key had been pressed.

title: The menus take no key from the app
statement: App command items MUST carry no accelerator, so every key reaches the app's keymap, with its overrides, unchanged.

title: Open Recent lists the last 10 folders
statement: File › Open Recent MUST list the recent folders, latest first, each opening its folder, then Clear Menu; with none it MUST say No Recent Folders.

title: Settings opens the app's settings in the focused window
statement: Settings… (Cmd+,) MUST open Appearance over the stage (`?panel=appearance`) in the focused product window.

title: The window has no system title bar; the app draws its own
statement: A window MUST have no system title bar. The app MUST draw its own 38 px bar across the top of the window, on the shell color (`--shell`) with no border, so the bar and the shell are one surface, and lay the page out under it. On macOS the traffic lights MUST float over the bar's left end, centered in its height; on Windows and Linux the native window controls MUST draw over its right end. The bar MUST leave room for them. The window MUST keep its title and, on macOS, its represented folder, which the Window menu and Mission Control show.

title: Back and forward follow the app's history
statement: The bar MUST start with back and forward buttons that run the app's `goBack` and `goForward` commands. Each MUST be disabled when there is no page to go to in that direction, where the browser can tell.

title: The command center names the page and opens quick find
statement: The bar's center MUST hold a command center: a pill showing the product name and the current page's heading ("Lathe — Add an item to the basket"), centered on the window and cut short with an ellipsis when it does not fit. Clicking it MUST open quick find (`quickOpen`), and its tooltip MUST show the shortcut.

title: The layout toggle shows and hides the navigation
statement: The bar MUST end with a toggle button for the navigation that runs `toggleNav`, the same command as the menus and the keys. It MUST say with `aria-pressed` whether the nav shows, and its tooltip MUST show the shortcut; while the nav is collapsed for space (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R18`), its tooltip and name MUST say so.

title: The bar drags the window, and a double-click zooms it
statement: Dragging the bar anywhere but on a control MUST move the window. Double-clicking it there MUST zoom or maximize the window, as the system's setting says. Its controls MUST take clicks and never drag.

title: The window's chrome follows the theme
statement: When the theme or the light or dark mode changes, including the system's appearance while the mode is System, the app MUST send the theme's shell and ink colors to the shell through `window.latheDesktop.setChrome`. The shell MUST then set the window's background and, on Windows and Linux, the window controls' colors.

title: In a browser there is no title bar
statement: The app MUST draw the title bar only when `window.latheDesktop` is present. In a browser the page MUST stay as it is.

title: A window opens on the shell color with a launch view until the specs answer
statement: A new window MUST show the theme's shell color at once and a launch view (the logo and "Opening <product>…") until the page has the product's specs, with no white flash and no blank window.

title: A folder the engine cannot load gets an error page with a way on
statement: When Lathe cannot start for a folder or the engine cannot load it, the window MUST show the message with Retry, Open Another Folder and Reveal in Finder.

title: A launch, error or About page runs only the buttons it shows
statement: A button press from the shell's own pages MUST run only when it is one of the actions that page shows, and only from that page.

title: About Lathe shows the versions and links to the repo and the record format
statement: About Lathe MUST open a small window with the app's, the engine's and Electron's versions and links to the repo and the record format, opened in the system browser. Check for Updates MUST NOT show until signed builds are published.

title: The app icon reads at every size and in light and dark Docks
statement: The app MUST have an icon drawn on Apple's icon grid, rendered from SVG for macOS (`.icns`, 16 to 1024 px), Windows (`.ico`) and Linux (PNGs), with a bolder drawing at 16 and 32 px. A development build (`npm run dev`) MUST show the icon with a "DEV" band in the Dock.

title: The Dock menu opens a new window and lists recent folders
statement: The Dock menu MUST have New Window, which runs Open Product Folder, and every folder opened MUST be added to the system's recent documents, which macOS lists in the Dock menu.

title: The Dock badge follows the window in front
statement: The badge MUST show the number of check errors of the focused product window's current space, its product's and the workspace's as its Checks panel counts them, or of the window focused last while another app is in front; it MUST follow that window when the data reloads or the space changes, and show nothing when there are none. A count MUST be a whole number from 0 up, from the window's own page; anything else MUST be ignored.

title: The graph is a stage of a page, not a place in the nav
statement: The graph MUST be reached as the stage of the page in hand (its button in the stage switch, Ctrl+G or Alt+G, Ctrl+1, the command palette), never as a separate item in the side navigation.

title: A group that is a record links; a group the app computes only folds
statement: A group that is a record (a capability, a use case, an aggregate) MUST link to its page wherever it heads its members; a stage or kind group MUST NOT pose as a record: its nav row only folds and its heading is not a link.

title: A selected row is the whole row
statement: In the nav, as in VS Code's explorer, a row MUST be as wide as the nav panel, indented by padding for its depth rather than by nested margins, with its indent guides and its fold chevron inside it. The current page's row MUST carry the selection over the whole row, from the panel's left edge over the indent and the chevron to its right edge, in the selection tint with its text and chevron in steel, with no bar of its own at its edge. A hovered row MUST take the hover tint over the whole row, and while the nav is used from the keyboard the selected and the focused row MUST show a 1 px steel outline. The lists stay nested for screen readers.

title: The menu lists each product and its domains
statement: The left menu MUST show each product as a space in its rail, and list the current space's domains (with their capabilities) in its panel.

title: The nav collapses to a rail, and is a full-screen sheet on a narrow screen
statement: A toggle MUST collapse the nav to a narrow rail of icons (the logo, Quick find, the spaces, Checks), each with a tooltip and an accessible name, and expand it again; the state MUST be remembered. When the window can't hold every open panel even with the wiki card collapsed, the nav MUST collapse to its rail for space, last (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R18`), leaving the remembered state alone. Under about 900 px wide the nav MUST become a full-screen sheet opened from the menu button in the top bar, with focus moved into it and kept inside it, and closed by Escape, its close button or choosing a page, with focus returned to the menu button.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: The nav folds by section and shows where you are
statement: The Tools section, and each domain and folder of the current space, MUST each fold and unfold with a chevron button carrying `aria-expanded`; the section holding the current page MUST open itself. The current space MUST have no heading of its own, since the rail names it: its first row is its overview. The current page MUST be marked clearly with `aria-current="page"` and scrolled into view. Icons MUST be inline line icons; counts MUST be quiet badges, with errors red and warnings amber on Checks; long names MUST be cut short with the full name as a tooltip; items MUST be at least 32 px high. A footer MUST say where the specs come from (the record format is a command and a link in the shortcuts sheet, as `LA-V65-R71` says).
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: The rail lists each product as a space
statement: The nav MUST have a rail about 56 px wide at its far left with one square icon per product in the products' ID order, and no item above every product. Each item MUST name itself in a tooltip.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The current space is marked
statement: The rail MUST mark the current space with an accent bar and `aria-current`.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The nav lists only the current space's things
statement: The nav MUST list the current space's product page, its domains, each folding into its five stages as the schema places kinds (with the capabilities in order under Use cases), and its groups (the product's other kinds of children), and MUST NOT list another product's domains.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: Choosing a space opens the last page visited in it
statement: Choosing a space MUST open the last page visited in that space during the session, or its product page when there is none.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: Alt and a number switch spaces
statement: Alt+1 to Alt+9 (⌥1 to ⌥9 on a Mac) MUST switch to the first nine spaces in rail order, and the command palette MUST offer a "Switch to <product>" command for each, with its keys. Every other shortcut MUST keep working.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The rail stays in the nav sheet on a narrow screen
statement: On a narrow screen the rail MUST stay visible inside the nav sheet.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: No view in a space shows another product
statement: Inside a space the header strip, the wiki card (its History included), the graph and its minimap, the ERD and Trace stages, hover cards, the reference's records and its "where the X are" links, saved tabs and the space's last page MUST show only that product, and the desktop Dock badge MUST count only its problems and the workspace's. A link into another product MUST NOT be drawn or listed, and another product's ID named in a text field MUST show as plain text, not as a link.
group_name: Work in one product at a time

title: The nav reads like stage folders
statement: Under the current space, the nav MUST list the product page; then Shared, only when it holds anything, holding the patterns, the standards and the records with no owner that two or more domains use, or none (one that a single domain uses sits in that domain, `LA-EXP-DS03`); then each domain, which unfolds into its five stages, then its open questions.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: Stages and folders fold one level at a time, with counts
statement: Every domain, stage and folder MUST be a foldable row showing one level when opened; only the level under the space MUST show by default. A stage with one folder MUST list that folder's records itself, with no folder row (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`). Each stage and folder MUST show its count of records, and one with no records MUST NOT be listed.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: The current page's branch opens itself
statement: Opening a page from the nav, or on the nav's first draw (a load, a reload, the nav expanded or opened as a drawer), MUST open the nav rows that hold it: a domain page its domain; a record page its domain and stage (or Shared), its folder when the stage has more than one, and the parents above it in that stage; a group page the folder of its kind. A page opened anywhere else (a link in the page, the graph, Back, quick find) MUST leave the nav's rows where they are (`LA-V61-R28`): the closed row that holds the page is marked instead, and opening that row opens the branch down to the page.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: Use cases lists capabilities, then use cases outside any
statement: A domain's Use cases stage, which holds only capabilities and so lists them itself (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`), MUST list the domain's capabilities in their order, then the use cases outside any capability; a capability's own use cases stay under it. A use case's flows MUST be listed in Interaction design and a requirement's tests in Test plan.
group_name: Read a product laid out in stage folders

title: Technical and test kind folders fold in the nav, with counts
statement: In the side nav, Technical specification's and Test plan's kind folders MUST be foldable rows with their counts, one level shown by default, and the current page's branch MUST open itself through its stage and kind folder. A kind folder's row MUST only fold. What is folded MUST last for the session.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: Records with no owner sit in the domain that uses them, or in Shared
statement: Records with no owner (value objects and their constraints, views and their requirements, integrations, UI components) MUST be listed in the one domain that uses them, or else in their product's Shared, by stage, and a specification in its domain's Domain model, in the nav and on the domain and product pages alike.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: The rail shows only with two or more products
statement: The space rail MUST show only when the workspace shows two or more products. With one, the nav MUST show no rail and its panel MUST take the rail's width, its first row the product's name and icon; collapsed, the nav MUST keep its buttons and list no spaces.

title: A domain has one page, at its ID
statement: A product's and a domain's only page MUST be their overview, at their bare ID (`/LA`, `/LA-EXP`); there MUST NOT be a second, generic record page for them. That one page MUST lose nothing the generic page showed: in the wiki card its text, kind, fields, data file, parent, children, links out and in, and problems.

title: The domain page groups records by stage
statement: The domain page MUST group its records by its five stages, each record under its parent where the parent is of the same stage (an aggregate's invariants, a use case's requirements).
group_name: Find a record in a domain

title: A search box filters records by ID or title
statement: The domain page MUST have a search box that filters the shown records by ID or title as the reader types.
group_name: Find a record in a domain

title: The domain page shows its coverage gaps and problems
statement: The domain page MUST list the domain's coverage gaps (each with the missing link) and the problems about its records.
group_name: Find a record in a domain

title: The domain page and group pages use the same folders as headings
statement: The domain page MUST head its records with the same stages and folders as the nav (the five stages), listing a folder's records directly or under one heading per kind when it holds several, a stage with one folder listing its records under the stage's own heading with no folder heading (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`), and keeping its one-level-deep folding. A group page MUST name the stage and folder of its kind, such as Interaction design.

title: Technical specification lists records by technical kind
statement: A domain's Technical specification MUST list its records by technical kind, in the plan's order (repositories, data models, tables, value types, predicates, event types, projections, command handlers, query handlers, event handlers, services, UI components, endpoint handlers, adapters, then the product's own kinds), each record with what it names in code: its file, or a table's name and storage.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: Test plan lists tests by test kind
statement: A domain's Test plan MUST list its tests by test kind in the plan's order (constraint, invariant, specification, policy, domain service, use case, view, endpoint, flow, integration, pattern rule and standard rule tests), each with its run by: its level, its file when automated, and its state.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: The domain page and group pages head the same groups
statement: The domain page MUST head Technical specification's and Test plan's kind groups with the same names and order as the nav, keeping its one-level-deep folding of records and its filter. A group page of tests MUST read them in the same groups.
group_name: Read the technical specification and test plan by kind

title: Endpoints and integrations sit in Interaction design
statement: The nav, the domain page and the graph MUST place an endpoint in its domain's Interaction design, and an integration in the Interaction design of the one domain whose flow steps exchange with it, or else of its product's Shared, by its kind's stage in the meta-model.

title: The domain page's coverage shows every obligation kind and the tests by state
statement: The domain page's Coverage section MUST show one group of bars per obligation kind the engine reports, the pattern rule line among them, each with designed, built, proved and not-automated-yet counts, then the domain's tests by state. Its gaps MUST name each obligation, pattern rules included, that the domain does not yet design, build or prove.

title: View and API requirements are listed under their view or endpoint
statement: The domain page MUST list each view requirement and API requirement nested under its view or endpoint, and each record of an obligation kind a product adds under its parent, with its gaps and problems on its row. Searching for one MUST keep its view or endpoint shown above it.

title: Each test shows its state, and one not automated yet never looks like proof
statement: The domain page MUST tag each test with its state. A test not automated yet MUST look unfinished and MUST NOT be counted or drawn as proof.

title: A domain page lists the patterns it follows
statement: A domain page MUST have a Patterns we follow section listing each pattern that the domain itself follows ("followed by the whole domain") or that any of its use cases follows, with the use cases that follow it. Each pattern's rules MUST be folded under its row, one level deep like the rest of the page, and each rule MUST show whether it applies in this domain (owed, not applicable or waived, LA-TRC-SP04) and, where owed, whether this domain proves it (the tests coverage counts as its proof there), both as the engine's coverage says and never worked out by the page itself, with a test not automated yet shown apart. A domain that follows no pattern MUST say so.

title: A rule the domain marks not applicable says so, with the use case and reason
statement: When a pattern rule names a setting and every use case in the domain that follows the pattern gives that setting a not-applicable reason, the rule MUST show as not applicable in that domain instead of its proof, naming each use case (as a link) and its reason.

title: A waived rule says Waived here, with the value the domain gives
statement: Where a pattern rule is waived in a domain, the domain page, the pattern page and the pattern rule page MUST show it there as "Waived here: <setting> is <value>", naming the value or values that domain's followers give the setting (or "not given"), instead of its proof, and the rule's Traceability gaps MUST leave that domain out. A rule's row MUST say what it applies when.

title: Every record ID shown is a link to that record
statement: Wherever a page shows a record ID, it MUST be a real link (`<a href>`) to that record's page, so any reference can be followed or opened in a new tab.

title: A wiki page shows one level below its record by default
statement: A wiki page (product, domain, record or group) MUST show by default only the records one level below the page's own record. Anything deeper MUST be folded under its row and open only when the person opens it, opens everything, or searches for something inside it.

title: A folded row keeps its count and its marks
statement: A folded row MUST still show how many records it holds ("4 requirements") and its own coverage marks and problem badge, so nothing hidden is forgotten.

title: A record ID named in text is a link in the text, never a relation
statement: A record ID named in a text field MUST be shown only as a link in the text: it MUST NOT appear among the record's links out or in, in the graph, or in coverage.

title: Code and links in text are shown as written
statement: Turning named IDs into links MUST NOT change text inside code blocks, links the author wrote, or code spans holding anything besides one ID; a code span holding one lone record ID is wrapped in the link with its code style kept, and it MUST run only on the sanitized HTML.

title: A row that leads to one record is one link to it
statement: A list row that leads to one record MUST hold exactly one link that stands for the whole row, and that link MUST be a real link (`<a href>`) to the record's page, so the row can be followed or opened in a new tab like any other reference. Other links in the row lead elsewhere and stay links of their own.

title: Links are shown by their labels, never by relation codes
statement: Wherever a page names a link, as a heading, a list title, a field label, an edge label or a tooltip, it MUST use the relation rule's `forward_label` read from the link's source or its `reverse_label` read from its target. A relation code such as `fulfills` or `hears` MUST NOT be shown as a heading or label; it may appear only as code, where a page explains how to write a link.

title: A page changes data only through its record actions
statement: A page MUST change a record only when the person acts on one of its record actions (Edit, Add or Remove), and then only by sending one write to `POST /api/write`, which the store's command layer applies or refuses whole. Until then a page MUST only read: `GET /api/spec`, and the Changes baseline from `GET /api/baseline` (LA-EXP-EP02). Opening, reading or searching a page MUST NOT send a write, and no page MUST write a data file itself, so every change is one the schema accepts and is reviewed in git.

title: A list of one kind is titled by that kind, through plural()
statement: A list of a record's children or a group's members MUST be titled by its kind's plural label, through `plural()`, when it holds one kind ("Invariants", "UC requirements", "Components"), and MUST be titled "Children" or "Members" only when it holds more than one kind to tell apart. Its count stays beside the title, and its accessible name and search box follow the title ("Invariants of LA-EXP-A1", "Filter domain rules"). A group's label MUST read as plain English, and any kind it names MUST come from the workspace's kind labels through `plural()`, such as "Command handlers", so a product that renames a kind sees its own name.

title: A refused change shows its reasons in place and changes nothing
statement: When the store refuses a write, the form or question MUST stay open with what the person entered, show every reason the store gave beside the input or section its command came from, and take focus to the reasons. Nothing on the page, and no data file, MUST change.

title: Steps are shown in their positions, as numbers
statement: A flow's steps MUST be shown in their `position`, compared as numbers (so step 10 comes after step 2), then by ID; the store refuses a step without a whole-number position, so none is ever hidden.

title: A step is always shown under its flow
statement: Wherever steps are shown, on a page or in the graph, each MUST be shown under the flow it belongs to, never as a record apart from it.

title: The record page shows the whole record, field by field
statement: The record page MUST show the record's ID, kind and title; its lead text (the one statement, goal, meaning or description its kind has), a test's When and Then as one scenario, and its notes, rendered as Markdown; its part rows laid out (an entity's or event's fields as a table, a flow's steps in order, a product's roles, a table's keys, a technical record's packages as one fact); its other columns as facts; and its parent and children.

title: The record page shows links both ways, grouped by relation
statement: The record page MUST show the record's outgoing links and its incoming links, each grouped by relation, with every linked record clickable.

title: A record's text is sanitized before it is shown
statement: The HTML rendered from a record's text fields MUST be sanitized before it is put on the page, because records are written by agents as well as people.

title: The record page shows the problems about it
statement: The record page MUST list every problem whose record is this one.

title: Anywhere on a record's row opens that record
statement: In every list of records (the rows of a product, domain, record or group page, coverage gaps, open questions, what a requirement fulfills, the patterns a domain follows, and the problems on the checks page), a click anywhere on a row MUST open the record the row leads to, not only a click on its ID or title. Cmd/Ctrl-click and middle-click MUST open it in a new tab. The row's other controls (its fold chevron, other record links, badges and buttons) MUST keep doing what they do. Keyboard focus stays on the row's one link, and its focus ring and hover cover the whole row; a tree's arrow keys work as before.

title: Record IDs named in text are links
statement: In a record's rendered text fields (a record page, and a product's or domain's overview), every ID-shaped token that is the ID of a record of the space, other than the record itself, MUST become a link to the record's address, its bare ID (`/<id>`), with the record's title on hover, and a plain click MUST move within the app. An ID inside a code block, an existing link or a code span with other text MUST NOT be linked, nor part of a longer ID; a code span holding exactly one such ID MUST link.

title: An ID that names no record stays plain text
statement: An ID-shaped token in a text field that is no record of the space MUST be shown as written, as plain text: it MUST NOT be a link, and nothing reports it, since no check reads text for IDs.

title: Every list that can grow stays at ten rows, in every view
statement: Every list that can grow, including a wiki page's lists (its children, links and problems) and a group page's members, MUST use the long list: ten rows, then a scroll inside with a search box and a count.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: Wiki pages open one level deep
statement: A product page MUST list its domains (and its summary and questions) but not their contents; a domain page its direct children grouped by kind (its five stages and open questions, each stage's kinds in the schema's order, and any other kind such as capabilities, in their `position`), each row showing its count of children; a record page its fields, its text, direct children and links; a group page its members. Each row with children MUST have a disclosure button (`aria-expanded`, a chevron) and each section an Expand all / Collapse all button. What is opened MUST be remembered for the session while moving around. A search inside a section MUST reveal matching nested records by opening their row just for the match. Right arrow MUST open a row (or move into it) and Left close it (or move to its parent). The command palette MUST offer Expand all and Collapse all for the page.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: Grouped requirements and rules read under their group headings
statement: The wiki MUST show a record's children that name a group, such as a use case's requirements, a view's view requirements, an endpoint's API requirements, a pattern's rules or a standard's rules, under their group headings: the ungrouped ones first, without a heading, then each group in the order it first appears. A use case's requirement table and a standard's rule table MUST head each group's rows with its name.
group_name: Read a record several ways at once

title: A flow's page shows its steps in order as a table
statement: A flow's record page MUST show its steps, when it has any, as a table in step order with the columns Step (order and ID), What happens (the title), Invokes, In view and Fulfills, each linked ID going to its record.
group_name: Read a flow step by step

title: A step's linked titles fold under its row
statement: Each step row MUST show one level: the step and the IDs it links to. The titles and kinds of what it invokes, happens in, exchanges with and fulfills MUST be folded under the row's disclosure, with Expand all and Collapse all for the table; a step has no text beyond its title.
group_name: Read a flow step by step

title: A step row shows its problems, and a flow without steps shows no table
statement: A step's row MUST carry a badge for its errors or warnings. A flow with no steps MUST NOT show a steps table.
group_name: Read a flow step by step

title: A flow with several paths shows a table per path
statement: When a flow's steps sit on more than one `path` (a step with no path is on the main path), its page MUST show each path as its own table, headed by the path's name, the main path first and then the others by name, each in its own step order, never interleaved by `position` across paths.
group_name: Read a flow step by step

title: A command's page lists its endpoint, and an endpoint's page its API requirements
statement: A command's or query's page MUST list the endpoint that exposes it among its children, with its method and route, and an endpoint's page MUST list its API requirements in a section with their count.
group_name: Read a domain's endpoints and integrations

title: An integration's page lists its exchanges and names its system
statement: An integration's page MUST list the flow steps that exchange with it, in a section with its count, saying which outside system it is when it names one
group_name: Read a domain's endpoints and integrations

title: Every record page has Edit, which opens its form in place
statement: Every record's page MUST offer Edit, Add and Remove as buttons in its record actions. Edit MUST open the record's form in place of the page's content, holding its columns, its parent, its links and its part rows as they are; Save MUST send every change as one write, and Cancel MUST leave the record as it was.

title: Inputs follow the schema, and pickers offer only valid targets
statement: Each input MUST take the type of its column (`LA-EXP-DS12`), an enum as a select of its values; the parent and each link MUST be picked from the records they may name, in the same product, and the form MUST say before it writes when a required input is empty or a value is not of its type.

title: A child is added from its parent's page
statement: Add MUST open an empty form for a record of a kind that may sit under the page's record (a choice of kind when several may), with that record as its parent and the next free ID suggested, and MUST add it in one write.

title: Remove asks first, naming what still references the record
statement: Remove MUST ask first, listing what still references the record (its children, the links into it, other records' rows that name it); while anything does, it MUST say the removal will be refused until those go. Confirming MUST send one write that removes the record with its part rows and the links it starts.

title: A refusal shows inline with its reasons
statement: A write the store refuses MUST show its reasons at the top of the form or question and beside the input each came from (`LA-V92-R10`), in the store's own words without a file and line, and the person MUST be able to fix the input and save again.

title: Editing works from the keyboard and a screen reader
statement: The record actions, the form and the remove question MUST work from the keyboard alone, as the rest of the app does: every input labeled, a required input marked as required, an input with a problem marked invalid and described by its message, focus taken to the form's first input when it opens and back to its action when it closes, and a change announced. They MUST pass the accessibility suite (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R10`) with no finding.

title: A test's page shows its state
statement: The record page MUST show a test's state; for a test not automated yet it MUST look unfinished and say that it does not count as proof.

title: The record content can sit inside another view
statement: A record's content (header, typed fields, parts, parent, children and links) MUST be one piece that takes a record ID and an `onNavigate` callback, apart from the page around it, so the graph can show it beside itself. Links inside it MUST go through `onNavigate` on a plain click and stay real links otherwise. It SHOULD read well at half the screen width.

title: Every list stays at 10 rows and can be searched
statement:
Every list in the spec pages (the menu's domains, a domain's record groups and nested lists, coverage gaps, problems and checks, open questions, a record's children and links both ways) MUST show up to 10 items as a plain list. With more than 10 it MUST show the first 10 rows' height and scroll inside, with a search box above it that filters by ID and title, a count such as "12 of 48", and a clear message when nothing matches.

The search box MUST be reachable with Tab, Escape MUST clear it, and the scrolling area MUST take focus so it scrolls from the keyboard. The list MUST know nothing about specs, so other views can use it.

title: A pattern page shows its settings, rules and followers
statement: A pattern's page (`/<id>`) MUST show a settings table (each setting and the rules that depend on it), its rules, and each domain that follows it with that domain's following use cases, the value each gives for each setting, and the domain's status for each rule as on the domain page. A pattern nobody follows MUST say that no domain owes its rules. The rules MUST NOT be listed a second time as plain children.

title: A pattern rule page shows the domains that owe it
statement: A pattern rule's page MUST list each domain that follows its pattern, with that domain's standing for the rule: proved, not automated yet, not proved, not applicable with the reasons, or waived.

title: An obligation lists what designs, builds and proves it
statement: An obligation's record page MUST show a Traceability section after its text and before its children, with these groups in this order, each left out when empty: Designed by, Built by (Met by, for a standard rule; each marked built or not built) and Proved by (each test with its state), holding exactly what the obligation's chain holds as the engine works it out, the chain the Trace stage draws, then its other incoming links under their reverse labels, then its links out under their forward labels, leaving out the records its chain already shows. The app MUST NOT work out a chain of its own. A group is titled by its links' label and holds each record once.

title: Each gap shows as a callout linked to its check
statement: An obligation's Traceability MUST name each gap in a callout, "Not designed yet", "Not built yet" or "Not proved yet", saying when its test is not automated yet, taken from coverage's own gaps for the domain that owes it, never from a count of its own, so it never disagrees with the coverage marks or the checks. Each callout MUST link to the page of the check that reports it (`not-designed`, `not-built`, `not-proved`). A pattern rule MUST show one line for each domain that owes it, judged from that domain's test alone.

title: A use case shows its requirements in a table
statement: A use case's Traceability MUST show a table with one row per UC requirement and the columns Requirement, Designed, Built and Proved, each cell linking the records that design, build or prove it and flagging a gap, followed by its flow and the patterns it follows.

title: A technical record and a test show what they implement, prove and run from
statement: A technical record's Traceability MUST show what it implements, then that record's tests, rolled up, then its other links under their labels. A test's MUST show what it proves (its parent), then its run by: its level, its state, and the file that runs it, flagged when the file is missing, or its manual reason. Any other kind MUST show its links out under their forward labels and its links in under their reverse labels.

title: Domain events show what raises them and what hears them
statement: An aggregate's page MUST list its domain events in their own list titled "Domain events", each row one link to the event saying which commands raise it and how many policies hear it, and its list of other children MUST NOT list them again. An event's page MUST show its fields (its `event_field` rows), as an entity's page shows its fields, and its Traceability MUST list "Raised by" and "Heard by"; a policy MUST list its event under "Hears". Every one of these words MUST come from the relations' labels in the schema.

title: Kinds, problem codes and columns link to their format pages
statement: The wiki card's kind line MUST link to the kind's page, on a record page and on a group page. Every problem's code on the Checks panel, the domain page and the record page MUST link to its check's page. A record's column labels MUST link to that column on its kind's page.

title: Standards sit in the technical specification and list their rules, what meets them and tests
statement: The nav MUST list a product's standards in the technical specification stage. A standard's page MUST list its rules in a table, one row each, with what meets each rule and the standard rule tests that prove it, and say when nothing does yet.

title: A standard rule shows what meets it and its tests
statement: A standard rule's Traceability MUST list what meets it under Met by and its standard rule tests under Proved by, and what meets it MUST list the rule under Meets. The reference MUST have a page for each standard kind, made from the schema.

title: A desktop record page offers its data file actions and a native menu
statement: In the desktop app a record page's facts MUST offer Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID for the data file that holds its row, and a right-click on its title, a record link or a graph node MUST ask for the native record menu, while a right-click elsewhere keeps the page's own. In a browser the page MUST show none of them.

title: Outcomes, data sets and a test's size and markers show on their pages
statement: A capability's page MUST list the business outcomes it serves; a test data set's page MUST show its environment, accounts, starting records, how to prepare and reset it, and the tests that start from it; a test's run by MUST show its size (small when it gives none) and its markers.

title: An outcome's page shows what measures it
statement: A business outcome's page MUST list the tests and records that measure it under Measured by, and how it is measured outside the code when it says so; a test's or record's page MUST list the outcomes it measures.

title: A use case lists its flows by interface, and a flow names its interface
statement: A use case's page MUST list its flows in a Flows by interface section, one row per flow with the name of the interface it goes through (and its kind when the name does not say it); a flow's page MUST name its interface under its title, as a link.

title: An interface lists its flows and the use cases with no flow through it
statement: An interface's page MUST list the flows through it under their capabilities, in the capabilities' order, one row per use case's flow, and then the product's use cases with no flow through it, under their capabilities too, both worked out from the flows and stored nowhere.

title: Motion carries no meaning and stops under reduced motion
statement: Motion in the graph MUST only help the eye follow a change: the view after a move MUST be the same with or without it, and when the system asks for reduced motion the camera MUST jump to the new view with no glide.

title: By touch, a tap selects a node and a second tap opens it
statement: A finger has no hover, so on a canvas a first tap on a node MUST select it and say what it is before anything moves, and only a second tap on the same node, or a tap on the card that names it, MUST open it. A pointer that can hover opens a node with one click.

title: A canvas stays mounted and is fitted before it paints
statement: The graph and the ERD stage MUST keep their canvas mounted while their content changes, MUST fit their first picture before it paints, and MUST NOT cut a glide short by fitting again when neither their size nor the open space has changed.

title: Domain events are flags
statement: Wherever a domain event is drawn as a node or box in the graph, it MUST be a flag, notched on the right (`LA-V93-R06`), in its stage's colors as every record is (`LA-V93-R12`), so events read the same in every layout.

title: A domain is drawn as a hexagon
statement: In the graph every domain node MUST be drawn as a hexagon, with flat top and bottom edges and pointed left and right ends, drawn as a polygon, not a rotated box. The points' chamfer MUST grow with the node's box scale (12 map units at box scale 1), at most a quarter of its width, so a very tall domain still reads as a hexagon and not as a diamond. Its border MUST follow the outline in every state, hovered, focused, keyboard-focused and selected by a tap, by coloring and thickening the outline's own edge, drawn inside the polygon.
